samples.text:
The flow chart shows how the applications for an undergraduate course in university are processed. There are eight steps from applying online to the enrolment.

Firstly, the student submit an online form with their grades and a personal statement. Then there is an eligibility check. If the application is not complete, it is returned to the student for correction. After that, the tutors review the application and give it a score.

Next, the applicants who are shortlisted are invited to an interview, which can be online or on campus. After the interview, the university make a decision. The student can get an offer, or be on the waiting list, or be rejected.

If the student has an offer, they accept it by confirming the place and paying a deposit. Then the final exam grades are checked against the offer. Finally, the student enrols and receives an ID card.

Overall, the process starts with the online application and finish with enrolment, and there are some points where the student cannot continue, for example if the application is rejected after the interview.
samples.why: Overview present but basic and placed last · every stage and outcome covered in order · mechanical linking · adequate vocabulary · several agreement, article and preposition errors that never block meaning.

samples.text:
The flow chart illustrates the procedure followed when students apply for an undergraduate course at university.

Overall, the process consists of eight stages, beginning with an online application and ending with enrolment. There are several points at which an applicant may not progress directly, since incomplete applications are returned and not every applicant receives an offer after the interview.

First, the student submits an online form together with their grades and a personal statement. The application is then checked for eligibility, and any incomplete ones are sent back to be corrected. Following this, tutors review and score each application, and those applicants who are shortlisted are invited to a interview, either online or on campus.

A decision is made after the interview: the applicant receives an offer, is placed on a waiting list or is rejected. Successful students accept the offer by confirming their place and paying a deposit. Later, their final exam grades are checked against the conditions of the offer. In the last stage, the student registers at the university and is given an ID card, which completes the process.
samples.why: Clear overview noting the points where applicants may not progress · logical sequencing with varied linkers · appropriate vocabulary (shortlisted, eligibility) · mostly error-free with one article slip.

samples.text:
The flow chart outlines how applications for undergraduate university courses are handled, from initial submission to final enrolment.

The procedure comprises eight stages and, although it is broadly linear, it contains several filtering points at which applicants may be returned, held back or turned down. Only those who satisfy each requirement ultimately enrol and receive a student ID card.

The process is initiated when a student submits an online application comprising their grades and a personal statement. This undergoes an eligibility check, with incomplete submissions being returned for correction. Eligible applications are then scored by tutors in an academic review, the first point at which the content of the application itself is judged, and shortlisted candidates are invited to an interview, which may take place online or on campus.

Following the interview, a decision is reached, with the applicant being made an offer, placed on a waiting list or rejected. Those who accept an offer confirm their place and pay a deposit, after which their final examination grades are checked against the terms of the offer. Once these are confirmed, the student enrols formally and is issued with an ID card.
samples.why: Skilful overview highlighting the filtering points · all stages and branches covered with precise sequencing · wide vocabulary (initiated, comprising, filtering) · varied complex passive structures · error-free.
